title: Check yourself: Error classes by type and origin

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A nightly job gets a 403 `permission_error` on every call after its key was moved to another workspace. What is the origin, and what is the first action?

options.text: Your account is at fault, so repair its access and do not retry
options.says: The table puts 403 under "Your access", and "a person has to act", so retrying is waste.

options.text: The provider is at fault, so retry with back-off until it clears
options.says: Ruled out because for the provider "something broke on their side", which is the 500 and 504 case.

options.text: Capacity is at fault, so wait for the retry-after interval
options.says: Ruled out because capacity means "the request was fine and the service could not take it now".

options.text: Your request is at fault, so repair the body and send it again
options.says: Ruled out because a 403 belongs to "Your credential or account", and a repaired body would meet the same refusal.

questions.stem: A request that carries a very large attachment returns a 413 `request_too_large`. Which action does the table give?

options.text: Wait for the retry-after interval, since this is a capacity error
options.says: Ruled out because capacity means "the request was fine and the service could not take it now", which a size refusal is not.

options.text: Retry with back-off, since the provider will probably recover soon
options.says: Ruled out because for the provider "something broke on their side", and a 413 is not that.

options.text: Shrink the payload below the documented ceiling, then send it again
options.says: The table lists 413 under "Your request size" with the action "Shrink it (32 MB limit on Messages)".

options.text: Resolve the conflict with a concurrent write, then try the call again
options.says: Ruled out because a conflict belongs to the "State of a resource" row, not to the size of the body.

concepts: The status table, as the page teaches it
